title: Cell Biology by the Numbers
result: Textbook, online edition read 2026-10-21 at book.bionumbers.org. Vignette 'What are the concentrations of different ions in cells?': in mammalian cells potassium is the dominant positive ion, at more than 10-fold the concentration of sodium, and outside the cell sodium dominates; potassium, about 10 to 30-fold more concentrated inside than outside, is usually close to electrochemical equilibrium in animal cells: its outward diffusion creates a potential difference that grows until it balances the diffusive flux, leaving the cell interior negative; in the extreme case of calcium the concentration outside is 10,000-fold that inside. Vignette 'What is the power consumption of a cell?', Table 1, adapted from Rolfe and Brown, Physiological Reviews 1997, rounded to one significant digit, with tissues described as rat ('rate tissues') in the caption and mouse in the text: share of the Na+/K+-ATPase in the oxygen consumption of tissues in the standard state, liver 5-10%, kidney 40-70%, heart 1-5%, brain 50-60%, skeletal muscle 5-10%.
